guitar.notes: Thorogood is known for using a Gibson ES-125-based custom guitar with a Bo Diddley-style rectangular body.

tone.target: thick slide blues-rock crunch with raw midrange bite
tone.profile: thick slide blues-rock crunch with raw midrange bite
tone.summary: A compact chain featuring a Boost for attack, Distortion for grit and sustain, followed by a UK 45 amp model with a vintage cabinet to deliver the required raw, midrange-heavy slide blues sound.

rig.name: George Thorogood & The Destroyers - Bad To The Bone - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Enhance the attack and midrange bite crucial for slide guitar.
Provide the necessary gritty crunch and sustain without sounding overly scooped.
blocks.gap: The RAT is excellent for mid-range bite, but a dedicated blues overdrive (like Green OD) might be closer. Using RAT for its aggressive midrange character.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-style crunch and raw British tone.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and fullness.
Further emphasize the raw midrange bite and cut any excessive low end.
A subtle tremolo can add character to slide playing, but kept off by default.
blocks.gap: The target tone is dry and raw. Tremolo is an optional addition for texture rather than core sound.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required 'small room' ambience without sounding wet or muddy.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the generic IR for a vintage, raw-sounding speaker to better capture the small room blues aesthetic.

proposals.recommendedAsset: vintage tweed or single-coil IR (e.g., Fender Deluxe/Blackface)
proposals.reason: The current 4x12 is too full; a vintage speaker will provide more raw, bite-y midrange.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and bite in the mids.
